column1: # Hyrule Warriors: Definitive Edition (Koei Tecmo's KTGL engine on NVN, SDK 3.5.1), update v65536 = 1.0.1.
# Started from the NSP script's provisional profile; the memory layout is the one it guessed, which boots and plays (not measured further).

# RomFS: loose files under data/ (tables of entries; the .gz names are not compressed), H.264 movies in movie/*.mp4 (no audio track decoded through the movie library), the music in sound/BGMProduct.g1l.
# The shaders are GLSLC compiler outputs: KTGL's G2S containers in data/action/shader/Normal.bin.gz, data/deferred/DeferredShader.bin.gz, the stage, shadow and effect files and the
# _SPK4100 post-effect packages (data/posteffect/*.kps), plus 7 built-in shaders the game compiles at boot with its own GLSLC (subsdk0), captured on the Mac (glslc_capture, in ps_other / vs_other).
# subsdk0 is GLSLC (NVN's run-time shader compiler), subsdk1 Nintendo's movie library (NintendoSDK_movie 3.5.1, OCTOPATH TRAVELER's build); sdk is OCTOPATH TRAVELER's build too
# The NPDM declares no system resource (META +0x14 = 0): no virtual address memory; nninitStartup sets a heap of the pool − used memory. The four modules take 43 MB, under the
# default 64 MB of used memory. About 3.4 GB resident and 1.9 GB of Metal allocations on the Mac in the first battle
# The game sets present interval 1 for its menus and battles and 2 for movies; its battles step by the time that passed (the mission clock and a 3 s stick hold match at 60 and 30 fps), so
# the default pacing keeps the game's own 60 fps
